name: Fixed-size sliding window
whenToUse: The standard answer: one pass and one running sum, no extra memory.

card.signals: "the average of all elements between i − k and i + k": every average is over a window of exactly 2k + 1 numbers in a row, and the windows of i and i + 1 share 2k numbers. "less than k elements before or after": windows that do not fit give -1.
card.pattern: a fixed-size window of size = 2k + 1. Build the first window once, then slide it one step at a time: one number enters on the right, one leaves on the left. The window [left, right] belongs to its centre, left + k.
card.coreIdea: keep total, the sum of the window. Each slide costs one addition and one subtraction. Fill avgs with -1 first, then write total // size at each centre. If size > n, nothing fits and avgs stays all -1.

invariant: After each slide, the window nums[left..right] has exactly size = 2k + 1 numbers, total is their sum, and its centre is left + k.
